subject: Private offer: regional list price adjustment and channel margin resolution
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@oriondata.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@oriondata.com
Date: 2026-06-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer cadence and regional list price question

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the call today. Procurement asked us to confirm whether the Azure private-offer list price in US-West needs to be adjusted separately from the global list price, and whether that would affect the channel uplift percentage we proposed to our reseller (CloudBridge).

Quick context: we need a two-tier commitment (base + burst) and CloudBridge requires at least a 15% net margin to keep their technical support allocation. Your last workbook had a global sticker and a single channel pass-through number — Procurement is asking for line-item clarity by region.

Can Redwood provide an updated breakdown (list price per region, private-offer net to Redwood, and suggested reseller uplift) so we can include it in our SOW? We can expedite sign-off if CloudBridge margin is preserved.

Appreciate the help — we aim to finalize by end of week.

Regards,
Samantha Price
Head of Procurement, Orion Data Labs
procurement@oriondata.com

Attachment: draft-sow-orion-v1.docx (referenced)

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@oriondata.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer cadence and regional list price question

Thanks Samantha — looping in Irene and Ben to align on channel math.

High level: we can publish a region-specific list price for US-West that does not change the base global model, and we can surface the reseller uplift as a separate line in the private-offer workbook. That keeps your public-facing pricing consistent while giving CloudBridge an explicit net uplift. Two quick ask items from our side:

- Confirm the exact CloudBridge uplift target (you mentioned 15% as a minimum).
- Confirm whether the burst tier should follow the same uplift or be negotiated as a separate surcharge.

Irene — can you validate whether the proposed per-region list price will impact our marketplace SKUs and whether there are any tax implications we should flag for Orion? Ben — can you draft the short version of the pass-through calculation (list -> Redwood net -> reseller uplift) so Samantha can forward to CloudBridge.

If we can get answers this afternoon I’ll push an updated az_private_offer_v2.xlsx.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer cadence and regional list price question

On Sat, Jun 12, 2026 at 1:48 PM Mateo Alvarez wrote:
> Irene — can you validate whether the proposed per-region list price will impact our marketplace SKUs and whether there are any tax implications we should flag for Orion?

Quick notes:
- Marketplace listing: Azure Marketplace supports price overrides per private offer; setting a US-West list price as a private-offer override is fine and won’t change the public SKU. We should ensure the SKU mapping includes the private-offer ID so billing teams route revenue correctly.
- Tax/VAT: US-West (US) has no additional VAT but state-level taxes may apply depending on Orion's billing address. Procurement should confirm the billing entity.
- Channel uplift: setting the reseller uplift as a separate line item in the private-offer is the cleanest path — call it "reseller pass-through" and include an evidence field for partner invoices. That preserves visibility for audits and keeps net revenue calculations straightforward.

Ben — I left a sample calculation in the shared drive (redwood_pricing_playbook_summary.pdf). It uses: list_price -> platform_fee (Redwood) -> reseller_pass_through -> final_net. If CloudBridge needs 15% on top of your final_net, we should show both gross and net amounts in the offer.

I can put together a redline of az_private_offer_v2.xlsx Monday morning with the required SKU tags.

— Irene
Director, Deal Operations, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@oriondata.com>, mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer cadence and regional list price question

Hi Samantha — thanks for the prompt answers on the call earlier. Attached is the quick-pass spreadsheet showing two scenarios:

Scenario A: Preserve CloudBridge 15% reseller margin by increasing the private-offer list_price for US-West by 6% (absorbs platform fee changes).
Scenario B: Keep list_price flat and add an explicit "reseller pass-through" line equal to 15% of Redwood net; this keeps the list price consistent across regions but shows CloudBridge their margin separately.

Recommendation: Scenario B is operationally simpler for Orion and CloudBridge (no SKU churn), and it keeps your public list prices unchanged. It also makes downstream invoice reconciliation easier because the pass-through is a labeled line in every invoice.

Next steps: 
- Samantha: confirm Scenario B acceptance and provide the billing entity for tax check.
- Orion Procurement: if ok, we’ll upload az_private_offer_v2.xlsx to the private-offer payload and share a DocuSign for the SOW.

I attached az_private_offer_v2.xlsx and the pricing summary PDF. Happy to walk CloudBridge & Procurement through the rows tomorrow (30 min).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

Attachments: az_private_offer_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_pricing_playbook_summary.pdf (summary)
